requirements.title: State of the art applied
requirements.statement: Technical solutions reflect the generally acknowledged state of the art for AI and functional safety; where an objective cannot be fully met, the approach taken to approach it is documented.
requirements.acceptance_criterion: State-of-the-art analysis names the standards/methods considered and justifies the chosen ones; deviations documented.
requirements.author: Catalogue author

requirements.title: AI component classified (usage level, technology class)
requirements.statement: Each AI software component in or for the safety-related system is classified by usage level (A1, A2, B1, B2, C, D) and AI technology class (I, II, III), using the most severe class where technologies are mixed, and the classification is documented.
requirements.acceptance_criterion: Documented usage level and technology class per component with justification; consistent with the project tags AI.usage_level and AI.tech_class.
requirements.assessor_guidance: Example: a CNN that detects persons in the hazard zone and whose failure can lead to a hazardous situation: usage level A1, class II.
requirements.author: Catalogue author
requirements.notes: Stand-alone requirement, selected through its source (D0026).

requirements.title: Requirement set matches the classification; learning mode permitted
requirements.statement: The component is developed to the requirement set assigned to its usage level and technology class; components inside the safety function (usage level A1/A2) learn offline only, and Class III components at A1/A2 have additional measures beyond the applied standard.
requirements.acceptance_criterion: Applied requirement set matches the classification; no online learning in A1/A2 components.
requirements.assessor_guidance: Offline retraining with re-verification before deployment remains possible as a maintenance activity.
requirements.author: Catalogue author
requirements.notes: Stand-alone requirement, selected through its source (D0026).

requirements.title: Usage level C component: no safety impact, adequate data quality
requirements.statement: A component at usage level C has no impact, including performance degradation, on the safety function, and adequate data quality is demonstrated.
requirements.acceptance_criterion: Impact analysis shows no effect on the safety function; data quality evidence available.
requirements.expected_evidence: Risk assessment / HARA; Data set documentation
requirements.author: Catalogue author
requirements.notes: Stand-alone requirement, selected through its source (D0026).

requirements.title: AI technology elements identified
requirements.statement: All technology elements involved in creating and executing the AI model — for training and for inference — are identified and documented and are part of the safety considerations.
requirements.acceptance_criterion: Element list covers the stack from application graph and model to compilers, libraries, executable code and computational hardware, separately for training and inference where they differ; each element is an assessment object (TE) or justified as out of scope.
requirements.assessor_guidance: Typical elements for camera-based person detection: trained detector (architecture + weights), training framework, model exchange format, graph compiler / inference engine, pre- and post-processing code, libraries, inference hardware (GPU/SoC/FPGA), camera interface. Create one TE object per element group with the same class (D0038).
requirements.author: Catalogue author
requirements.notes: Derived requirement (rule A8), stand-alone (D0026).

requirements.title: Technology element classified and treated per class
requirements.statement: Each technology element is classified and developed and verified with the methods appropriate to its class.
requirements.author: Catalogue author
requirements.notes: Derived requirement (rule A8), stand-alone (D0026).

requirements.title: Technology element: usage level and class assigned
requirements.statement: The element has a usage level (A1, A2, B1, B2, C, D) and a technology class (I, II, III) with justification, and the standards and complementary methods applicable to it are named.
requirements.acceptance_criterion: Classification matrix element → usage level → class → applicable standard / methods, with rationale (e.g. whether the parameters are hand-crafted, verifiable after creation or too complex to analyse).
requirements.assessor_guidance: Typical result: trained model Class II (complementary methods of TR 5469 clauses 9-11 and of the applied AI standard); inference engine, pre-/post-processing, libraries Class I (IEC 61508-3 with Annex A interpretation); hardware Class I (IEC 61508-2). Class III elements are not relied upon for risk reduction.
requirements.author: Catalogue author
requirements.notes: Derived requirement (rule A8), stand-alone (D0026).

requirements.title: Technology element developed with the methods of its class
requirements.statement: Class I elements follow the existing functional-safety standards (for software: IEC 61508-3 techniques as interpreted for AI elements); for Class II elements the part not achievable with those standards is addressed by complementary methods (additional verification and validation); higher-level elements (model, application graph) are treated with the AI-specific properties, lower-level elements with non-AI properties.
requirements.acceptance_criterion: For Class I: selected IEC 61508-3 techniques per table with interpretation for AI elements; for Class II: reference to the complementary methods applied (data, model, V&V requirements of the project); no element left without treatment.
requirements.assessor_guidance: Annex A of TR 5469 interprets IEC 61508-3 Tables A.1-A.19: most techniques apply to use-case-independent elements (libraries, runtime); traceability, coding standards and structural coverage are difficult for the model itself; stateless design is not appropriate for AI elements. For a Class II element the CI is assessed against the complementary methods only.
requirements.author: Catalogue author
requirements.notes: Derived requirement (rule A8), stand-alone (D0026).

requirements.title: Three-stage realisation principle applied
requirements.statement: Desirable properties, the methods addressing them and the resulting acceptance criteria are derived for each stage of the realisation principle and combined in an overall acceptance argument.
requirements.author: Catalogue author
requirements.notes: Derived requirement (rule A8), stand-alone (D0026).

requirements.title: Desirable properties defined per stage
requirements.statement: Desirable properties are defined for data acquisition, knowledge induction (training) and processing / output generation, case by case from the application, the technology and the properties in existing standards and TR 5469 clause 8.
requirements.acceptance_criterion: List of properties per stage with justification of selection and of omitted clause-8 properties; mapping to the relevant standards.
requirements.assessor_guidance: Examples for person detection: specifiability, generalisation, robustness (lighting, contamination), domain shift, verifiability, interpretability, confidence (cf. TR 5469 Annex B Tables B.1, B.3).
requirements.author: Catalogue author
requirements.notes: Derived requirement (rule A8), stand-alone (D0026).

requirements.title: Properties related to topics, methods and techniques
requirements.statement: Each property is related to topics and to the detailed methods and techniques that address it.
requirements.acceptance_criterion: Property → topic → method/technique table; every selected property has at least one method; methods trace to the project requirements (CRs) that verify them.
requirements.assessor_guidance: Annex B Table B.4 shows the expected depth (topic, details, compliance criteria).
requirements.author: Catalogue author
requirements.notes: Derived requirement (rule A8), stand-alone (D0026).

requirements.title: Acceptance criteria and overall acceptance argument
requirements.statement: Acceptance criteria (criteria for the selected methods, metrics, thresholds such as uncertainty limits) are identified from the methods and embedded in an overall acceptance argument (e.g. assurance case) that is consistent with technology-independent risk acceptance criteria.
requirements.acceptance_criterion: Criteria per stage tailored to the usage level and class; overall argument (e.g. GSN assurance case) links stage criteria to the integrity target of the safety function; risk acceptance principle (ALARP, GAMAB, MEM, ...) named.
requirements.assessor_guidance: Example: stage 1 image-quality metrics; stage 2 recall per HARA scenario at stated confidence; stage 3 response time and zone classification; argument shows the combination meets the PL/SIL of the safety function.
requirements.author: Catalogue author
requirements.notes: Derived requirement (rule A8), stand-alone (D0026).

requirements.title: Risk management process over the lifecycle
requirements.statement: A risk management process is established, implemented, documented and maintained as a continuous, iterative process over the entire lifecycle, with regular systematic review and updating.
requirements.acceptance_criterion: Documented RM procedure/plan with lifecycle scope, review triggers and records of at least one review cycle.
requirements.assessor_guidance: Look for review triggers beyond placing on the market: field data, incidents, model/data updates, ODD changes.
requirements.author: Catalogue author

requirements.title: Limits, intended purpose and foreseeable misuse determined
requirements.statement: The limits of the product are determined: intended purpose incl. specific context and conditions of use, lifecycle phases, and reasonably foreseeable misuse incl. misuse arising from interaction with other systems and other AI systems.
requirements.acceptance_criterion: Limits and misuse cases documented and traceable into the hazard identification.
requirements.assessor_guidance: Person detection: mounting heights, distances, lighting, PPE, body postures, occlusion, other optical systems.
requirements.author: Catalogue author

requirements.title: Hazards identified incl. AI-specific hazard sources
requirements.statement: Known and reasonably foreseeable hazards and hazardous situations are identified, including AI-specific sources: performance insufficiency, data bias affecting health and safety, distribution shift/ODD exit, feedback effects and adversarial manipulation.
requirements.acceptance_criterion: Hazard list covers generic and AI-specific sources; each hazard traceable to risk estimation.
requirements.author: Catalogue author

requirements.title: Risks estimated
requirements.statement: Risks are estimated from severity and probability, for intended use and reasonably foreseeable misuse.
requirements.acceptance_criterion: Estimation method defined and applied to every identified hazard.
requirements.author: Catalogue author

requirements.title: Risks evaluated; residual risk acceptable
requirements.statement: Risks are evaluated against defined acceptability criteria; the residual risk per hazard and the overall residual risk are judged acceptable.
requirements.acceptance_criterion: Acceptability criteria documented before evaluation; per-hazard and overall residual-risk judgement recorded.
requirements.author: Catalogue author

requirements.title: Risk reduction in the order of priority
requirements.statement: Risks are eliminated or reduced by applying protective measures in the order: inherently safe design, protective measures, information for use.
requirements.author: Catalogue author

requirements.title: Inherently safe design
requirements.statement: Hazards are eliminated or risks minimised by design and development as far as technically feasible.
requirements.acceptance_criterion: Design measures listed per hazard with their effect on the risk.
requirements.author: Catalogue author

requirements.title: Protective and mitigation measures
requirements.statement: Protective, mitigation and control measures address the risks that cannot be eliminated by design.
requirements.acceptance_criterion: Each residual risk after design has a protective/mitigation measure or a justification.
requirements.author: Catalogue author

requirements.title: Information on residual risks and training needs
requirements.statement: Users are informed of residual risks; need for training and personal protective equipment is identified and stated.
requirements.acceptance_criterion: Every residual risk accepted with "information" is traceable to the IFU; training needs stated.
requirements.expected_evidence: Risk assessment / HARA; Instructions for use
requirements.author: Catalogue author

requirements.title: Combined effect of measures considered
requirements.statement: The combined effects and interactions of the measures taken for the different requirements are considered.
requirements.acceptance_criterion: Analysis of interactions between measures (e.g. robustness vs availability, oversight vs automation) documented.
requirements.author: Catalogue author

requirements.title: Users' knowledge and context considered
requirements.statement: Risk reduction takes into account the technical knowledge, experience, education and training to be expected of the deployer/operator and the presumable context of use.
requirements.acceptance_criterion: User profile documented and used in measure selection.
requirements.author: Catalogue author

requirements.title: Vulnerable persons considered
requirements.statement: Likely adverse impact on persons under 18 and other vulnerable groups is considered.
requirements.acceptance_criterion: Vulnerable groups identified or their absence justified.
requirements.author: Catalogue author

requirements.title: Fundamental-rights risks
requirements.statement: Risks to fundamental rights are identified and evaluated.
requirements.acceptance_criterion: FR risk analysis documented.
requirements.author: Catalogue author

requirements.title: Post-market data fed back into risk management
requirements.statement: Risks emerging from post-market monitoring data are evaluated and fed back into the risk assessment.
requirements.acceptance_criterion: Procedure links PMM outputs to RM review; evidence of at least one evaluation or planned trigger.
requirements.expected_evidence: PMM plan / records; Risk assessment / HARA
requirements.author: Catalogue author

requirements.title: Hazards from intended self-evolution assessed
requirements.statement: Hazards that may arise during the lifecycle as an intended evolution of self-evolving behaviour or logic are included in the risk assessment.
requirements.acceptance_criterion: Evolution envelope defined and hazards of foreseeable evolution analysed.
requirements.author: Catalogue author

requirements.title: Risks from interaction within assemblies
requirements.statement: Risks resulting from interactions between machinery arranged and controlled to function as an integral whole are assessed.
requirements.acceptance_criterion: Interfaces to host machine / other machinery analysed.
requirements.author: Catalogue author

requirements.title: Abnormal use prevented by design
requirements.statement: Foreseeable abnormal use that would engender a risk is prevented by design.
requirements.acceptance_criterion: Misuse cases with design countermeasures or justification.
requirements.author: Catalogue author

requirements.title: Applicable requirements determined
requirements.statement: The risk assessment determines which essential requirements apply to the product.
requirements.acceptance_criterion: List of applicable requirements with justification for non-applicable ones.
requirements.author: Catalogue author

requirements.title: Use of AI justified against alternatives
requirements.statement: Alternative realisations of the necessary risk reduction (incl. non-AI solutions) are considered, and the AI-based solution is confirmed (or another chosen) by comparing residual risks; the safety hierarchy is followed.
requirements.acceptance_criterion: Documented comparison of alternatives with residual risk and selection rationale.
requirements.assessor_guidance: Typical alternatives: conventional ESPE (light curtain, laser scanner), guards, speed and separation monitoring with certified sensors.
requirements.author: Catalogue author
requirements.notes: Stand-alone requirement, selected through its source (D0026).

requirements.title: AI fault analysis
requirements.statement: An AI fault analysis identifies potential AI faults, assesses their risk and is maintained over the life cycle.
requirements.author: Catalogue author
requirements.notes: Stand-alone requirement, selected through its source (D0026).

requirements.title: AI fault list derived
requirements.statement: A list of potential AI faults is derived and documented with their causes, covering at least faults from model creation (specification, data, model complexity), inputs (malicious input, drift, disturbances), pre-processing, model insufficiencies and the AI monitor.
requirements.acceptance_criterion: Fault list covers the reference categories or justifies their exclusion; each fault has documented causes.
requirements.author: Catalogue author
requirements.notes: Stand-alone requirement, selected through its source (D0026).

requirements.title: Risk assigned to each AI fault
requirements.statement: Each AI fault has a risk based on severity (considering the usage level) and probability of occurrence of its triggering condition, estimated qualitatively or quantitatively.
requirements.acceptance_criterion: Every listed fault has severity, probability and resulting risk with method stated.
requirements.author: Catalogue author
requirements.notes: Stand-alone requirement, selected through its source (D0026).

requirements.title: AI fault list maintained
requirements.statement: The AI fault list is extended over time, top-down from application knowledge and bottom-up from root-cause analysis of test results and field incidents.
requirements.acceptance_criterion: Procedure and evidence of updates from tests or field data.
requirements.author: Catalogue author
requirements.notes: Stand-alone requirement, selected through its source (D0026).

requirements.title: AI fault mitigation measures selected and implemented
requirements.statement: For every AI fault with unacceptable risk, avoidance and/or control measures are selected according to the measure ratings of the applied AI standard for the usage level and the required systematic capability (or alternatives of demonstrated equal effectiveness), implemented, and the fault analysis is repeated to confirm acceptable residual risk.
requirements.acceptance_criterion: Traceability fault -> measure -> effectiveness; all highly recommended measures applied or omission justified; re-analysis after measures documented.
requirements.author: Catalogue author
requirements.notes: Stand-alone requirement, selected through its source (D0026).

requirements.title: AI-relevant hazardous scenarios identified in ODD terms
requirements.statement: The hazard and risk analysis identifies the hazardous scenarios to which the AI function contributes, each with a unique identifier and described in terms of ODD attributes so that the corresponding data and tests can be identified.
requirements.acceptance_criterion: List of AI-relevant hazardous scenarios with IDs covering the ODD; each scenario expressed with ODD attributes; traceable to safety requirements with quantitative targets.
requirements.assessor_guidance: Example scenarios: person in the protective zone not detected; person detected too late; person entering from an occluded area; crouching or lying person.
requirements.author: Catalogue author
requirements.notes: Derived requirement (rule A8), stand-alone (D0026).

requirements.title: Technology maturity assessed
requirements.statement: The maturity of the AI technologies used is assessed for the application context; unknown risks of immature technology are treated, and risk awareness for mature technology is maintained by risk monitoring with field data, awareness training and maintenance.
requirements.acceptance_criterion: Maturity assessment per key technology (evidence of use in comparable safety applications, known limitations); resulting measures and monitoring documented.
requirements.author: Catalogue author
requirements.notes: Derived requirement (rule A8), stand-alone (D0026).

requirements.title: Fault model per AI system element
requirements.statement: A fault model is defined for each element of the AI system description (at least data sets, annotation, ML model, learning process, deployment toolchain, inference runtime and hardware, pre-/post-processing, link between ML and safety life cycle); failure modes are identified per element (e.g. HAZOP guide words) and at the component output; the analysis is complete with respect to the fault model, and fault effects are assessed by injection where the fault is precise enough, otherwise by analysis.
requirements.acceptance_criterion: System element description; fault-model specification with rationale for the abstraction level; worksheets per element; output failure modes defined; injection plan and results; failure modes traced to safety requirements and mitigations.
requirements.assessor_guidance: Output failure modes for detection: omission, commission, wrong localisation, late detection, temporal inconsistency. Guide-word examples: data "less" = under-represented ODD stratum; "other than" = wrong label; "more" = duplicates or train/test leakage. Deployment faults: quantisation deviations, sensor degradation, bit flips.
requirements.author: Catalogue author
requirements.notes: Derived requirement (rule A8), stand-alone (D0026).

requirements.title: PFMEA of the offline training process
requirements.statement: A process FMEA covers the offline ML development process from data acquisition to release of the deployed inference artefact; failure modes, effects on the safety function, causes and prevention/detection controls are identified and rated, and actions above a defined priority threshold are tracked; classification FMEA is considered for classification-based perception.
requirements.acceptance_criterion: Process description; PFMEA worksheet with ratings; action list with status; evidence of implemented controls.
requirements.assessor_guidance: Steps: acquisition, annotation, split, augmentation, pre-processing, training, model and threshold selection, evaluation, export/conversion, release. Typical failure modes: under-represented groups (children, wheelchair users, crouching persons), inconsistent annotation guide, train/test leakage, test data used for tuning, augmentation removing safety-relevant features, pre-processing mismatch training vs deployment, wrong checkpoint released, non-representative quantisation calibration data.
requirements.author: Catalogue author
requirements.notes: Derived requirement (rule A8), stand-alone (D0026).

requirements.title: Operational design domain specified
requirements.statement: The operational design domain (operating environment and conditions) of the AI function is specified, incl. geographical, contextual, behavioural and functional setting and its limits.
requirements.acceptance_criterion: ODD specification under configuration control; limits measurable.
requirements.assessor_guidance: Person detection: illumination range, distances, field of view, person sizes/poses, PPE, occlusion, contamination of optics, background clutter.
requirements.author: Catalogue author

requirements.title: Drift of ODD parameters analysed and managed
requirements.statement: Expected drift of ODD parameters and of application requirements during operation is analysed for its safety impact; mitigations are implemented for unacceptable risks and training data are updated when safety-related shifts are detected.
requirements.acceptance_criterion: Drift analysis with risk evaluation and mitigations; where the applied standard rates this measure, the required effectiveness level is reached.
requirements.author: Catalogue author
requirements.notes: Stand-alone requirement, selected through its source (D0026).

requirements.title: Operational domain bounded for data and test design
requirements.statement: The operational domain is specified with boundaries that are as exact as practicable, described by the space of possible inputs or by a real-world usage profile, including limits of use, environmental, location and temporal limits and the allocation of responsibilities between system, users and other systems; it is the reference domain for data sets, simulation and real-world tests.
requirements.acceptance_criterion: ODD specification under configuration control; attribute taxonomy with value ranges or classes used as common vocabulary for labelling, coverage analysis and test design; behaviour at and beyond the boundary defined; responsibilities allocated; reviewed before data collection. Specification covers the geographical, contextual, behavioural and functional setting of use; limits measurable.
requirements.assessor_guidance: Attributes e.g.: environment (indoor hall), illuminance range, distance to person, person type (adult, child, wheelchair, crouching), occlusion, clothing contrast, camera contamination. Out-of-ODD example: illuminance below the lower limit → machine stops.
requirements.author: Catalogue author
requirements.notes: Derived requirement (rule A8), stand-alone (D0026).

requirements.title: Environment complexity and specification vagueness analysed
requirements.statement: The complexity of the operating environment and the vagueness of the specification are analysed for their effect on safety; the strategy for functional completeness (detailed specification, data covering the environment, or both) is stated, and model adequacy and prediction uncertainty are considered in behaviour planning.
requirements.acceptance_criterion: Complexity factors listed with their impact on the AI function; completeness strategy and residual vagueness documented; uncertainty handling defined.
requirements.assessor_guidance: Factors e.g.: varying natural/artificial light, reflective surfaces, shadows, multiple persons, partial occlusion, clothing variation, children vs adults.
requirements.author: Catalogue author
requirements.notes: Derived requirement (rule A8), stand-alone (D0026).

requirements.title: Test strategy across development
requirements.statement: Testing is planned and performed at appropriate points throughout development and in any event before placing on the market, to select risk measures and to confirm consistent performance and compliance.
requirements.acceptance_criterion: Test plan with test levels, timing and entry/exit criteria; records show execution before release.
requirements.author: Catalogue author

requirements.title: Safety functions testable in use
requirements.statement: The user can test the safety functions; special equipment, accessories and functional test procedures needed for safe testing, adjustment and maintenance are supplied.
requirements.acceptance_criterion: Functional test procedure in IFU; test aids supplied where needed.
requirements.author: Catalogue author

requirements.title: AI test methods selected per integrity level
requirements.statement: Test methods adequate to the AI faults and their risk are selected and applied for the target integrity level, with a rationale for substitutes and combinations.
requirements.author: Catalogue author
requirements.notes: Created from ISO/IEC TS 22440-1 (CD) (D0025). Source-specific applicability and guidance are in the TS coverage links (D0046).

requirements.title: Tests: statistical performance on a representative test set
requirements.statement: The performance of the AI function is assessed statistically on a representative test set, to the extent required for the integrity level, or the omission or substitution is justified.
requirements.acceptance_criterion: Test records available; the methods required for the integrity level are performed, recommended methods are performed or their omission is justified.
requirements.author: Catalogue author
requirements.notes: Created from ISO/IEC TS 22440-1 (CD) (D0025). Source-specific applicability and guidance are in the TS coverage links (D0046).

requirements.title: Tests: ODD coverage (inside, outside and near the boundary)
requirements.statement: Tests inside the ODD, outside it and near its boundary are performed to the extent required for the integrity level, or the omission or substitution is justified.
requirements.acceptance_criterion: Test records available; the methods required for the integrity level are performed, recommended methods are performed or their omission is justified.
requirements.author: Catalogue author
requirements.notes: Created from ISO/IEC TS 22440-1 (CD) (D0025). Source-specific applicability and guidance are in the TS coverage links (D0046).

requirements.title: Tests: scenario-based (nominal and hazardous)
requirements.statement: Scenario-based tests of nominal and hazardous situations are performed to the extent required for the integrity level, or the omission or substitution is justified.
requirements.acceptance_criterion: Test records available; the methods required for the integrity level are performed, recommended methods are performed or their omission is justified.
requirements.author: Catalogue author
requirements.notes: Created from ISO/IEC TS 22440-1 (CD) (D0025). Source-specific applicability and guidance are in the TS coverage links (D0046).

requirements.title: Tests: corner cases
requirements.statement: Corner-case tests are performed to the extent required for the integrity level, or the omission or substitution is justified.
requirements.acceptance_criterion: Test records available; the methods required for the integrity level are performed, recommended methods are performed or their omission is justified.
requirements.author: Catalogue author
requirements.notes: Created from ISO/IEC TS 22440-1 (CD) (D0025). Source-specific applicability and guidance are in the TS coverage links (D0046).

requirements.title: Tests: out-of-distribution inputs
requirements.statement: Tests with out-of-distribution inputs are performed to the extent required for the integrity level, or the omission or substitution is justified.
requirements.acceptance_criterion: Test records available; the methods required for the integrity level are performed, recommended methods are performed or their omission is justified.
requirements.author: Catalogue author
requirements.notes: Created from ISO/IEC TS 22440-1 (CD) (D0025). Source-specific applicability and guidance are in the TS coverage links (D0046).

requirements.title: Tests: replay of recorded data
requirements.statement: Recorded field or test data is replayed to the AI function to the extent required for the integrity level, or the omission or substitution is justified.
requirements.acceptance_criterion: Test records available; the methods required for the integrity level are performed, recommended methods are performed or their omission is justified.
requirements.author: Catalogue author
requirements.notes: Created from ISO/IEC TS 22440-1 (CD) (D0025). Source-specific applicability and guidance are in the TS coverage links (D0046).

requirements.title: Tests: robustness (input corruption, metamorphic, combinatorial)
requirements.statement: Robustness tests (e.g. input corruption, metamorphic and combinatorial testing) are performed to the extent required for the integrity level, or the omission or substitution is justified.
requirements.acceptance_criterion: Test records available; the methods required for the integrity level are performed, recommended methods are performed or their omission is justified. Robustness tests cover environmental variation, sensor faults and interaction cases defined in the ODD.
requirements.author: Catalogue author
requirements.notes: Created from ISO/IEC TS 22440-1 (CD) (D0025). Source-specific applicability and guidance are in the TS coverage links (D0046).

requirements.title: Tests: distributional shift
requirements.statement: Tests under distributional shift are performed to the extent required for the integrity level, or the omission or substitution is justified.
requirements.acceptance_criterion: Test records available; the methods required for the integrity level are performed, recommended methods are performed or their omission is justified.
requirements.author: Catalogue author
requirements.notes: Created from ISO/IEC TS 22440-1 (CD) (D0025). Source-specific applicability and guidance are in the TS coverage links (D0046).

requirements.title: Tests: bias and fairness
requirements.statement: Bias and fairness tests are performed to the extent required for the integrity level, or the omission or substitution is justified.
requirements.acceptance_criterion: Test records available; the methods required for the integrity level are performed, recommended methods are performed or their omission is justified.
requirements.author: Catalogue author
requirements.notes: Created from ISO/IEC TS 22440-1 (CD) (D0025). Source-specific applicability and guidance are in the TS coverage links (D0046).

requirements.title: Tests: adversarial inputs
requirements.statement: Tests with adversarial inputs are performed to the extent required for the integrity level, or the omission or substitution is justified.
requirements.acceptance_criterion: Test records available; the methods required for the integrity level are performed, recommended methods are performed or their omission is justified.
requirements.author: Catalogue author
requirements.notes: Created from ISO/IEC TS 22440-1 (CD) (D0025). Source-specific applicability and guidance are in the TS coverage links (D0046).

requirements.title: Tests: synthetic test cases
requirements.statement: Synthetically generated test cases are used to the extent required for the integrity level, or the omission or substitution is justified.
requirements.acceptance_criterion: Test records available; the methods required for the integrity level are performed, recommended methods are performed or their omission is justified.
requirements.author: Catalogue author
requirements.notes: Created from ISO/IEC TS 22440-1 (CD) (D0025). Source-specific applicability and guidance are in the TS coverage links (D0046).

requirements.title: Tests: formal verification
requirements.statement: Formal verification methods are applied to the extent required for the integrity level, or the omission or substitution is justified.
requirements.acceptance_criterion: Test records available; the methods required for the integrity level are performed, recommended methods are performed or their omission is justified.
requirements.author: Catalogue author
requirements.notes: Created from ISO/IEC TS 22440-1 (CD) (D0025). Source-specific applicability and guidance are in the TS coverage links (D0046).

requirements.title: Tests: decisions based on causally relevant features
requirements.statement: It is validated that the decisions of the AI function rely on causally relevant features, to the extent required for the integrity level, or the omission or substitution is justified.
requirements.acceptance_criterion: Test records available; the methods required for the integrity level are performed, recommended methods are performed or their omission is justified.
requirements.author: Catalogue author
requirements.notes: Created from ISO/IEC TS 22440-1 (CD) (D0025). Source-specific applicability and guidance are in the TS coverage links (D0046).

requirements.title: Test completeness and validation effort assessed
requirements.statement: Completeness of tests or simulations and the validation effort in the final application are assessed.
requirements.acceptance_criterion: Completeness and effort assessment documented. Test plan defines test levels, timing and entry/exit criteria; execution before release is recorded.
requirements.author: Catalogue author
requirements.notes: Stand-alone requirement, selected through its source (D0026).

requirements.title: Installed AI-based safety function validated
requirements.statement: Correct implementation is checked at installation and the safety function is validated in the target application, including its behaviour and exclusion of unintended behaviour as planned.
requirements.acceptance_criterion: Commissioning / validation records.
requirements.author: Catalogue author
requirements.notes: Stand-alone requirement, selected through its source (D0026).

requirements.title: Independent functional-safety assessment considered
requirements.statement: An independent functional-safety assessment is considered according to the applied functional-safety standard.
requirements.acceptance_criterion: Decision and, where performed, assessment report.
requirements.author: Catalogue author
requirements.notes: Stand-alone requirement, selected through its source (D0026).

requirements.title: Coverage metrics for data and V&V established early
requirements.statement: Metrics checking that the data sets and the V&V activities (incl. simulation and real-world tests) correspond to the operational domain and to the hazardous scenarios are defined with targets and evaluation points before training.
requirements.acceptance_criterion: Data/V&V plan with metrics (ODD attribute coverage, combinatorial coverage, per-scenario sample counts, match to the usage profile), targets and evaluation points (e.g. each data-set release); applied to data sets and to simulation and physical campaigns.
requirements.author: Catalogue author
requirements.notes: Derived requirement (rule A8), stand-alone (D0026).

requirements.title: System-level testing (virtual and physical)
requirements.statement: System-level testing complements component-level V&V, combining virtual and physical testing.
requirements.author: Catalogue author
requirements.notes: Derived requirement (rule A8), stand-alone (D0026).

requirements.title: Test strategy and allocation of test objectives
requirements.statement: Component- and system-level tests are planned; each system-level test is classified as data-based (open-loop) or scenario-based (closed-loop); each test objective and HARA scenario is allocated to component tests, simulation or physical tests with rationale; effects hard to simulate are covered physically.
requirements.acceptance_criterion: Test strategy; allocation matrix of HARA scenarios and safety requirements against test levels and environments, every scenario allocated at least once; list of effects not represented in simulation with their physical coverage.
requirements.assessor_guidance: Not adequately simulated, e.g.: motion blur, camera auto-exposure lag, end-to-end latency camera-to-stop.
requirements.author: Catalogue author
requirements.notes: Derived requirement (rule A8), stand-alone (D0026).

requirements.title: System-level test scenario catalogue
requirements.statement: Executable test scenarios are derived from the HARA scenarios allocated to system level, with the ODD attributes as parameters, all reasonable variations and stress scenarios; the parameter sampling method and the number of runs and repetitions are justified statistically from target failure rates and confidence.
requirements.acceptance_criterion: Catalogue with parameters, ranges and distributions traceable to HARA scenarios and ODD attributes; variation coverage per scenario or justified gaps; sampling rationale linked to the safety analysis; run and repetition numbers with statistical justification.
requirements.assessor_guidance: Sampling e.g.: importance sampling around the stopping-distance boundary, constrained random over illuminance × person type × clothing; repeated stopping tests against the predefined limit. Synthetic frames for component tests are test data, not catalogue scenarios.
requirements.author: Catalogue author
requirements.notes: Derived requirement (rule A8), stand-alone (D0026).

requirements.title: System-level tests executed and results meet the requirements
requirements.statement: All catalogue scenarios are executed in their allocated environment with the required runs; failures are analysed and closed before release; simulation results are correlated with physical results and used in the safety argument only where the toolchain is qualified for the objective.
requirements.acceptance_criterion: Execution report with traceability scenario → environment → result; executed vs required runs; failure list with root cause and closure; failed runs not removed by re-running without analysis; reference to toolchain qualification for each virtual result used.
requirements.author: Catalogue author
requirements.notes: Derived requirement (rule A8), stand-alone (D0026).

requirements.title: Structured physical testing
requirements.statement: Structured physical tests of known scenarios are performed in controlled set-ups and in the final operating environment, derived from safety, technology and product analysis, with measurements tracked over time; tests that cannot be performed safely use surrogates or virtual testing.
requirements.acceptance_criterion: Physical test specification and set-up (environment control, measurement, tracking); results incl. KPI achievement in real conditions; list of tests replaced by surrogates or simulation.
requirements.assessor_guidance: Use dummies for collision-relevant scenarios and persons only for non-hazardous behaviour.
requirements.author: Catalogue author
requirements.notes: Derived requirement (rule A8), stand-alone (D0026).

requirements.title: Virtual testing toolchain qualified
requirements.statement: Where virtual test results support the safety argument, the virtual testing toolchain is set up, verified, validated and qualified for its purpose.
requirements.author: Catalogue author
requirements.notes: Derived requirement (rule A8), stand-alone (D0026).

requirements.title: Virtual testing toolchain: set-up and documentation
requirements.statement: The toolchain combines the needed simulation types (MIL, SIL, HIL) with the same scenarios across levels, records ground truth and metadata (versions, seeds, parameters) per run, and its design is documented for review.
requirements.acceptance_criterion: Allocation of objectives to MIL/SIL/HIL with shared scenario set; run logs with ground truth and metadata; toolchain documentation.
requirements.assessor_guidance: N/A – feature absent if no virtual (simulation, digital-twin, MIL/SIL/HIL) test results are used in the safety argument.
requirements.author: Catalogue author
requirements.notes: Derived requirement (rule A8), stand-alone (D0026).

requirements.title: Virtual testing toolchain: fitness for purpose and capability
requirements.statement: Test objectives, boundary conditions and requirements per simulation model are defined; assumptions, limitations, fidelity levels and fidelity KPIs with tolerances are stated, and the risks from inaccuracy and incompleteness of the simulation environment are assessed.
requirements.acceptance_criterion: Model requirements derived from the ODD; fidelity KPIs with tolerances; risk assessment with mitigations; for perception, arguments on rendering realism.
requirements.assessor_guidance: N/A – feature absent if no virtual (simulation, digital-twin, MIL/SIL/HIL) test results are used in the safety argument.
requirements.author: Catalogue author
requirements.notes: Derived requirement (rule A8), stand-alone (D0026).

requirements.title: Virtual testing toolchain: correctness (verification)
requirements.statement: The implementation of the simulation models is verified by code verification, calculation verification and sensitivity analysis.
requirements.acceptance_criterion: Verification results; sensitivity analysis without implausible jumps.
requirements.assessor_guidance: N/A – feature absent if no virtual (simulation, digital-twin, MIL/SIL/HIL) test results are used in the safety argument.
requirements.author: Catalogue author
requirements.notes: Derived requirement (rule A8), stand-alone (D0026).

requirements.title: Virtual testing toolchain: accuracy (validation)
requirements.statement: The toolchain is validated against real-world data from subsystem models (environment, sensor, actuation) up to the integrated system; simulation-to-reality correlation is within the defined tolerance.
requirements.acceptance_criterion: Validation results per step; correlation analysis of simulated vs physical results; resulting model improvements or restrictions of use.
requirements.assessor_guidance: N/A – feature absent if no virtual (simulation, digital-twin, MIL/SIL/HIL) test results are used in the safety argument.
requirements.author: Catalogue author
requirements.notes: Derived requirement (rule A8), stand-alone (D0026).

requirements.title: Virtual testing toolchain: criticality and qualification
requirements.statement: The criticality of each simulation tool and model for the safety argument is analysed and tools are qualified where required (IEC 61508-3 or ISO 26262-8).
requirements.acceptance_criterion: Tool classification / confidence level per tool and model with qualification evidence.
requirements.assessor_guidance: N/A – feature absent if no virtual (simulation, digital-twin, MIL/SIL/HIL) test results are used in the safety argument.
requirements.author: Catalogue author
requirements.notes: Derived requirement (rule A8), stand-alone (D0026).

requirements.title: Fault injection and timing simulation
requirements.statement: Timing simulation and fault injection are applied to the AI-based safety function, with faults injected at system, component and sub-component level (sensors, communication, timing, compute platform) including combinations not reachable in real-world testing.
requirements.acceptance_criterion: Fault-injection plan and results covering the levels and relevant combinations; timing results show requirements met under worst-case load.
requirements.assessor_guidance: Faults e.g.: frame drops, pixel defects, lens contamination, corrupted buffers, communication loss to the safety controller, delayed inference; combination frame drop + low light.
requirements.author: Catalogue author
requirements.notes: Derived requirement (rule A8), stand-alone (D0026).

requirements.title: Findings and incidents fed back to HARA and test suite
requirements.statement: Newly discovered hazards from tests, field monitoring and reported incidents are assessed, fed back into the HARA and the safety solution, and added to the qualification scenario suite.
requirements.acceptance_criterion: Procedure for assessing findings; updated HARA traceable to the finding; new requirements or measures implemented and re-verified; scenario suite updated.
requirements.expected_evidence: Risk assessment / HARA; PMM plan / records
requirements.author: Catalogue author
requirements.notes: Derived requirement (rule A8), stand-alone (D0026).

requirements.title: Test oracles adequate
requirements.statement: Expected results (test oracles) are obtained reliably: where back-to-back testing provides them, the independence of the compared versions is assessed; where no reliable oracle exists, alternative well-tested implementations or simulation are used, or the design separates the risks from the model.
requirements.acceptance_criterion: Oracle source per test set; independence assessment for back-to-back testing; justification where oracles are derived.
requirements.expected_evidence: V&V / test report; Data set documentation
requirements.author: Catalogue author
requirements.notes: Derived requirement (rule A8), stand-alone (D0026).

requirements.title: AI performance specified, verified and consistent
requirements.statement: The AI function achieves an appropriate, specified level of accuracy for its intended purpose, verified against prior-defined statistical criteria, and performs consistently throughout its lifecycle.
requirements.assessor_guidance: Tension: MR wording is absolute ("shall not lead to hazardous situations"); AIA accepts probabilistic thresholds. Acceptance must be derived from the required risk reduction (PL/SIL, or the systematic capability required by the applied AI standard).
requirements.author: Catalogue author

requirements.title: Performance metrics selected and justified
requirements.statement: Performance metrics are selected and their appropriateness for the safety function is justified.
requirements.acceptance_criterion: Metric set documented with justification per safety-relevant output (e.g. false-negative rate).
requirements.author: Catalogue author

requirements.title: Acceptance thresholds prior-defined
requirements.statement: Acceptance thresholds (incl. probabilistic thresholds and confidence) are defined before testing and derived from the required risk reduction.
requirements.acceptance_criterion: Thresholds dated before test execution; derivation documented.
requirements.author: Catalogue author

requirements.title: Verified performance meets thresholds
requirements.statement: Test results across the ODD and the relevant hazardous scenarios meet the thresholds with stated statistical confidence.
requirements.acceptance_criterion: All scenarios meet thresholds at the stated confidence; deviations dispositioned.
requirements.author: Catalogue author

requirements.title: Performance consistent over the lifecycle
requirements.statement: Performance is monitored and maintained over the lifecycle (degradation, drift, updates).
requirements.acceptance_criterion: Monitoring indicators and thresholds for re-validation defined.
requirements.author: Catalogue author

requirements.title: Runtime uncertainty quantification
requirements.statement: Uncertainty-estimation techniques are considered for AI fault avoidance and control; where runtime uncertainty estimates are used, they are specified, cover out-of-ODD, domain-shift and in-domain uncertainty, and their accuracy is evaluated with adequate metrics.
requirements.acceptance_criterion: Specification and calibration evidence (e.g. Brier score) where used.
requirements.author: Catalogue author
requirements.notes: Stand-alone requirement, selected through its source (D0026).

requirements.title: Uncertainty quantification to verify performance after training
requirements.statement: Uncertainty quantification is used to verify the performance of the trained model.
requirements.acceptance_criterion: Uncertainty-based verification documented where applied, or the omission justified.
requirements.author: Catalogue author
requirements.notes: Created from ISO/IEC TS 22440-1 (CD) (D0025). Source-specific applicability and guidance are in the TS coverage links (D0046).

requirements.title: Statistical demonstration of residual failure rate
requirements.statement: The acceptable residual failure metric and the required performance metric are derived from the safety-function target and demonstrated statistically.
requirements.author: Catalogue author
requirements.notes: Stand-alone requirement, selected through its source (D0026).

requirements.title: Residual failure target derived and validated
requirements.statement: The residual failure metric allowed for the AI system is derived from the failure target of the safety function, taking its architecture into account, and the residual failure rate is validated quantitatively against it.
requirements.acceptance_criterion: Derivation documented; validation result meets the target. Targets and thresholds documented (dated) before the verification tests are run.
requirements.assessor_guidance: Typical chain: PFH of the safety function -> allowed dangerous detection failures per hour -> required per-frame recall given exposure assumptions.
requirements.expected_evidence: Safety requirements specification; V&V / test report
requirements.author: Catalogue author
requirements.notes: Stand-alone requirement, selected through its source (D0026).

requirements.title: Required performance metric derived with rationale
requirements.statement: The required performance metric of the AI component is systematically derived and quantified from the residual failure target, with a rationale for the derivation.
requirements.acceptance_criterion: Quantified metric with documented derivation. Metric set selected with a justification of its appropriateness for the safety function (e.g. false-negative rate per safety-relevant output).
requirements.author: Catalogue author
requirements.notes: Stand-alone requirement, selected through its source (D0026).

requirements.title: Performance demonstrated with statistical confidence
requirements.statement: The performance metric is expressed as a probability distribution from empirical data; the confidence value matches the target integrity, and confidence bounds are within the order of magnitude of the required metric.
requirements.acceptance_criterion: Statistical evaluation with confidence value and interval (or hypothesis test). Results meet the required metric across the ODD and the relevant hazardous scenarios at the stated confidence; deviations dispositioned.
requirements.author: Catalogue author
requirements.notes: Stand-alone requirement, selected through its source (D0026).

requirements.title: Residual failures without systematic pattern
requirements.statement: Residual failures are analysed to show they have no considerable systematic pattern.
requirements.acceptance_criterion: Error analysis across ODD dimensions and scenarios without significant clusters, or clusters addressed.
requirements.author: Catalogue author
requirements.notes: Stand-alone requirement, selected through its source (D0026).

requirements.title: Data sets meet quality criteria
requirements.statement: Training, validation and testing data sets meet the quality criteria (governance, representativeness, setting, special-category safeguards); for systems not trained on data, the criteria apply to test data sets.
requirements.author: Catalogue author

requirements.title: Data governance and management practices
requirements.statement: Data sets are subject to governance and management practices appropriate to the intended purpose.
requirements.author: Catalogue author

requirements.title: Design choices
requirements.statement: Relevant design choices for the data are documented.
requirements.acceptance_criterion: Design choices and rationale documented.
requirements.expected_evidence: Data management plan; Data set documentation
requirements.author: Catalogue author

requirements.title: Collection and origin
requirements.statement: Data collection processes and the origin of data (and, for personal data, the original purpose) are documented.
requirements.acceptance_criterion: Provenance recorded per data source.
requirements.expected_evidence: Data management plan; Data set documentation
requirements.author: Catalogue author

requirements.title: Preparation operations
requirements.statement: Data-preparation operations (annotation, labelling, cleaning, updating, enrichment, aggregation) are defined and controlled.
requirements.acceptance_criterion: Labelling guide and QA records exist.
requirements.expected_evidence: Data management plan; Data set documentation
requirements.author: Catalogue author

requirements.title: Assumptions
requirements.statement: Assumptions about what the data measure and represent are formulated.
requirements.acceptance_criterion: Assumptions documented and reviewed.
requirements.expected_evidence: Data management plan; Data set documentation
requirements.author: Catalogue author

requirements.title: Availability, quantity, suitability
requirements.statement: Availability, quantity and suitability of the needed data sets are assessed.
requirements.acceptance_criterion: Assessment documented incl. sufficiency argument.
requirements.expected_evidence: Data management plan; Data set documentation
requirements.author: Catalogue author

requirements.title: Bias examination
requirements.statement: Data are examined for biases likely to affect health and safety (or fundamental rights), especially where outputs influence future inputs.
requirements.acceptance_criterion: Bias analysis per safety-relevant attribute.
requirements.expected_evidence: Data management plan; Data set documentation
requirements.author: Catalogue author

requirements.title: Bias measures
requirements.statement: Measures to detect, prevent and mitigate identified biases are applied.
requirements.acceptance_criterion: Measures and their effect documented.
requirements.expected_evidence: Data management plan; Data set documentation
requirements.author: Catalogue author

requirements.title: Data gaps
requirements.statement: Data gaps or shortcomings preventing compliance are identified and addressed.
requirements.acceptance_criterion: Gap list with disposition.
requirements.expected_evidence: Data management plan; Data set documentation
requirements.author: Catalogue author

requirements.title: Data relevant, representative, error-free, complete
requirements.statement: Data sets are relevant, sufficiently representative, as free of errors and complete as possible, with appropriate statistical properties for the persons/conditions concerned.
requirements.acceptance_criterion: Coverage and quality metrics per data set against the ODD.
requirements.author: Catalogue author

requirements.title: Data reflect the setting of use
requirements.statement: Data sets take into account the specific geographical, contextual, behavioural or functional setting of intended use.
requirements.acceptance_criterion: Mapping of data attributes to ODD parameters with coverage evidence.
requirements.author: Catalogue author

requirements.title: Special-category data safeguards
requirements.statement: Special categories of personal data are processed for bias detection/correction only under the conditions and safeguards of AIA Art 4a(1).
requirements.acceptance_criterion: Necessity justification and safeguards documented, or confirmation that no special-category data are processed.
requirements.author: Catalogue author

requirements.title: Datasets archived for reproducibility
requirements.statement: Training, verification and validation datasets are retained as evidence of correct creation and to reproduce the system behaviour.
requirements.acceptance_criterion: Versioned datasets retrievable and linked to the released model version.
requirements.author: Catalogue author
requirements.notes: Stand-alone requirement, selected through its source (D0026).

requirements.title: Data properties, metrics and data requirements
requirements.statement: Relevant data properties are measured with data quality metrics, data requirements are derived from them and verified, and test data requirements support the needed statistical significance.
requirements.author: Catalogue author
requirements.notes: Stand-alone requirement, selected through its source (D0026).

requirements.title: Relevant data properties identified and measured
requirements.statement: Relevant data properties are identified (expert judgement, standards, law), measured with data quality metrics (quantitative where reasonably practicable) and enforced by data quality measures.
requirements.acceptance_criterion: Property list with metrics and measured values; the effectiveness required for the integrity level is reached. The property set covers at least relevance, representativeness, errors (incl. labels), completeness and statistical properties for the persons and conditions concerned; shortcomings are listed.
requirements.author: Catalogue author
requirements.notes: Created from ISO/IEC TS 22440-1 (CD) (D0025). Source-specific applicability and guidance are in the TS coverage links (D0046).

requirements.title: Data requirements derived
requirements.statement: Data requirements with target values are derived from the relevant data properties and the ODD.
requirements.acceptance_criterion: Requirements traceable to properties and ODD. ODD-based requirements cover the geographical, contextual, behavioural and functional setting of intended use.
requirements.author: Catalogue author
requirements.notes: Stand-alone requirement, selected through its source (D0026).

requirements.title: Data requirements verified at the end of the pipeline
requirements.statement: Data requirements are verified at the last stage of the data pipeline, on the data actually used.
requirements.acceptance_criterion: Verification records from the final pipeline stage. Preparation operations (annotation, labelling, cleaning, updating, enrichment, aggregation) are defined (e.g. labelling guide) and their output is verified.
requirements.expected_evidence: Data set documentation; V&V / test report
requirements.author: Catalogue author
requirements.notes: Stand-alone requirement, selected through its source (D0026).

requirements.title: Test data requirements
requirements.statement: Requirements for verification, validation and test data cover at least ODD coverage, ODD representativeness and independence from training data; targets for data quantity, label error rate, coverage and representativeness follow from the needed statistical significance; re-use of test data is limited or overfitting monitored, and validation uses unseen data.
requirements.acceptance_criterion: Test data specification with targets and evidence of independence and limited re-use.
requirements.author: Catalogue author
requirements.notes: Stand-alone requirement, selected through its source (D0026).

requirements.title: Data management system
requirements.statement: A data management system over the life cycle protects the data, keeps it intact and makes changes traceable, with configuration and change control of provenance, access rights and data quality metrics.
requirements.acceptance_criterion: System in place; change history and access control evidenced.
requirements.author: Catalogue author
requirements.notes: Stand-alone requirement, selected through its source (D0026).

requirements.title: Training data enhancement / augmentation
requirements.statement: Where real application data cannot achieve the required properties at adequate effort, training (and test) datasets are enhanced by augmentation, generative alteration or synthetic data.
requirements.acceptance_criterion: Enhancement methods documented with their effect on the data properties; the effectiveness required for the integrity level is reached. Every identified data gap has a documented disposition (enhancement or justification).
requirements.author: Catalogue author
requirements.notes: Created from ISO/IEC TS 22440-1 (CD) (D0025). Source-specific applicability and guidance are in the TS coverage links (D0046).

requirements.title: Synthetic test data justified
requirements.statement: Synthetic test data supplement insufficient real data; where they replace real-world testing, the distribution shift is analysed and transferability shown by similar mean performance and error patterns on real and synthetic data.
requirements.acceptance_criterion: Transferability analysis documented where synthetic data replace real tests.
requirements.assessor_guidance: N/A – feature absent if no synthetic test data are used.
requirements.expected_evidence: Data set documentation; V&V / test report
requirements.author: Catalogue author
requirements.notes: Stand-alone requirement, selected through its source (D0026).

requirements.title: Label errors of test data accounted for
requirements.statement: Where label errors affect the performance evaluation, the rate of wrong labels in the test data is determined and added to the residual failure rate; boundary and edge-case test data are manually verified (recommended).
requirements.acceptance_criterion: Label error rate determined and included in the residual failure estimate.
requirements.expected_evidence: Data set documentation; V&V / test report
requirements.author: Catalogue author
requirements.notes: Stand-alone requirement, selected through its source (D0026).

requirements.title: Data sets designed and checked against the HARA (criteria a-c)
requirements.statement: Training and test data are designed and checked against the AI-relevant hazardous scenarios: scenarios mapped to data attributes, test data covering each risk and its variations, and sufficient volume and diversity per risk-causing situation.
requirements.author: Catalogue author
requirements.notes: Derived requirement (rule A8), stand-alone (D0026).

requirements.title: HARA scenarios mapped to data attribute sets (a)
requirements.statement: For each AI-relevant hazardous scenario, the set of data attributes identifying the corresponding data is specified so that its presence in the training, validation and test sets can be checked; depth according to the requirement level.
requirements.acceptance_criterion: Traceability matrix scenario → attribute set (query) → data subsets; 100 % of AI-relevant scenarios mapped or the scenario justified and covered by other measures; annotation schema carries the attributes needed.
requirements.assessor_guidance: Requirement level (Annex C.2) — low: causes of deterioration examined and reflected in attributes; middle: + system-level risk analysis and documented attribute decisions; high: + review of past results and FTA. Example: "person not detected in protective zone" → {person present, in zone, distance ≤ x m}; if occlusion is not labelled, the occlusion scenario cannot be verified.
requirements.expected_evidence: Data set documentation; Risk assessment / HARA
requirements.author: Catalogue author
requirements.notes: Derived requirement (rule A8), stand-alone (D0026).

requirements.title: Test data cover each risk, its variations and combinations (b)
requirements.statement: For each identified risk, test data exist for its attribute set and cover all reasonable variations of the risk-causing situations; the distribution of the other attributes is analysed for unintended bias; the required attribute combinations are defined with combinatorial test design; gaps and biases are closed by additional or synthetic data or rebalancing, or justified.
requirements.acceptance_criterion: Per-scenario inventory of required variations with sample counts and gap list; distribution and bias analysis per scenario with safety-impact assessment; defined and achieved combinatorial coverage (e.g. pair-wise) or justified gaps; gap-closure records; safety claims not based solely on unvalidated synthetic data. Biases likely to affect health and safety are examined; measures against them and their effect are documented.
requirements.assessor_guidance: Requirement level (Annex C.3) — low: inputs for each major risk attribute and serious combinations; middle: pair-wise coverage of relevant risk factors; high: coverage strength set per risk. Bias example: all low-light samples show adults in bright clothing → {low light × dark clothing × child} missing.
requirements.expected_evidence: Data set documentation; V&V / test report
requirements.author: Catalogue author
requirements.notes: Derived requirement (rule A8), stand-alone (D0026).

requirements.title: Test data volume and diversity per risk-causing situation (c)
requirements.statement: For each risk-causing situation, the test data are sufficiently diverse within the attribute values; the collection and preparation processes are assessed for introduced bias; the required volume is determined from the intended probability of risk mitigation and the training data needs; uncontrolled factors causing distribution shift are addressed.
requirements.acceptance_criterion: Diversity indicators per situation (locations, sessions, persons, cameras, near-duplicate rate) meet the data plan; process assessment of collection, filtering, annotation (guidelines, inter-annotator agreement) and pre-processing; required vs available independent samples per situation with statistical justification, or limited safety claim; each uncontrolled factor covered in data, restricted by the ODD or monitored in the field. Biases likely to affect health and safety are examined.
requirements.assessor_guidance: Requirement level (Annex C.4) — low: unbiased sources and sampling, sufficient data per case; middle: + occurrence probabilities and distribution check; high: + coverage indicators, no spurious correlations. Volume example: FNR ≤ 0.5 % at 95 % confidence with zero misses needs about 600 independent samples per situation (n ≈ 3/p).
requirements.expected_evidence: Data set documentation; V&V / test report
requirements.author: Catalogue author
requirements.notes: Derived requirement (rule A8), stand-alone (D0026).

requirements.title: Single faults do not lead to hazardous situations
requirements.statement: A fault in the hardware or the logic of the safety-related control system does not lead to a hazardous situation.
requirements.acceptance_criterion: Fault analysis (FMEA/FTA) shows safe reaction to each relevant fault; architecture meets required integrity level.
requirements.author: Catalogue author

requirements.title: Protective-device failure leads to safe state
requirements.statement: The absence or failure of a component of the protective device prevents starting or stops the hazardous movement.
requirements.acceptance_criterion: Failure modes of device components (incl. camera, compute, AI component) lead to stop / no start.
requirements.author: Catalogue author

requirements.title: Resilience to errors, faults and environment
requirements.statement: The AI function is as resilient as possible to errors, faults and inconsistencies within the system or its environment, incl. interaction with persons and other systems, and to external influences.
requirements.acceptance_criterion: Robustness tests cover environmental variation, sensor faults and interaction cases defined in the ODD.
requirements.author: Catalogue author

requirements.title: AI logic errors detected and controlled
requirements.statement: Errors of the AI/control logic do not lead to hazardous situations: abnormal inputs/outputs (e.g. out-of-distribution, low confidence) are detected and lead to a safe reaction.
requirements.acceptance_criterion: Detection mechanisms specified and verified; safe reaction defined.
requirements.author: Catalogue author

requirements.title: Power and communication disturbances
requirements.statement: Interruption, re-establishment or fluctuation of the power supply or of communication/wireless connections does not lead to a hazardous situation.
requirements.acceptance_criterion: Power-cycle, brown-out and communication-loss tests passed.
requirements.author: Catalogue author

requirements.title: System-level failure analysis of the AI-based safety function
requirements.statement: A failure analysis of the elements realising the AI-based safety function (e.g. FTA, FMEA) determines subsystem safety requirements and the effects of AI faults from data acquisition, knowledge induction and output generation in the overall system context.
requirements.acceptance_criterion: Analysis covers all elements and AI fault sources; where the applied standard rates this measure, the required effectiveness level is reached.
requirements.author: Catalogue author
requirements.notes: Stand-alone requirement, selected through its source (D0026).

requirements.title: Architecture of the AI-based safety function chosen and analysed
requirements.statement: The architecture of the AI-based safety function is chosen in the hazard and risk analysis and system design, considering the usage level and technology class, AI fault tolerance and how the systematic capability of its elements combines, and the AI faults connected to it are determined.
requirements.acceptance_criterion: Architecture documented with rationale and associated AI faults.
requirements.author: Catalogue author
requirements.notes: Stand-alone requirement, selected through its source (D0026).

requirements.title: Safe non-AI back-up function
requirements.statement: A back-up function realised without AI maintains or reaches a safe state when a failure of the AI part is detected.
requirements.acceptance_criterion: Back-up function specified, implemented and its switch-over tested.
requirements.author: Catalogue author
requirements.notes: Stand-alone requirement, selected through its source (D0026).

requirements.title: AI monitor limits and checks the AI output
requirements.statement: An AI monitor (non-AI or AI-based) limits the output using physical boundaries or a priori knowledge and/or checks its plausibility using expected output, temporal behaviour, uncertainty information and independent sources; a non-AI limiter yields an acceptable output range for each input; the monitor's effectiveness is evaluated.
requirements.acceptance_criterion: Monitor specified, implemented and its effectiveness evaluated.
requirements.author: Catalogue author
requirements.notes: Stand-alone requirement, selected through its source (D0026).

requirements.title: Redundant / diverse AI channels
requirements.statement: Where diverse redundancy is used, the voting/aggregation of outputs is specified, common-cause input conditions are analysed and controlled, overall performance metrics are defined, and an analysis of effectiveness, sensitivity and undetectable faults is in the technical documentation.
requirements.acceptance_criterion: Redundancy analysis and CCF measures documented; performance metrics defined.
requirements.author: Catalogue author
requirements.notes: Stand-alone requirement, selected through its source (D0026).

requirements.title: Runtime monitors specified and their impact analysed
requirements.statement: For each runtime monitor (input, output, internal state, AI monitor) the behaviour is specified and its impact on the system is analysed: detected fault types and sensitivity, fault signatures, monitor performance and intervention after detection.
requirements.acceptance_criterion: Specification and impact analysis per monitor.
requirements.author: Catalogue author
requirements.notes: Stand-alone requirement, selected through its source (D0026).

requirements.title: Input filtering / pre-processing
requirements.statement: Pre-processing or filtering of the input stream to remove unwanted input is considered and, where used, applied consistently to training and validation data.
requirements.acceptance_criterion: Decision documented; filters specified and verified where used.
requirements.author: Catalogue author
requirements.notes: Stand-alone requirement, selected through its source (D0026).

requirements.title: Random hardware faults of the AI execution platform analysed
requirements.statement: Random hardware failures of the hardware executing the AI technology (affecting control flow, memory, inputs or outputs) are analysed with the fault models of the functional-safety standards and controlled by hardware safety measures.
requirements.acceptance_criterion: Hardware fault analysis (e.g. FMEDA) of the inference platform incl. accelerators and memory; diagnostics and hardware metrics consistent with the integrity target.
requirements.assessor_guidance: Fault models e.g. IEC 61508-2 Annex A, ISO 26262-11 for semiconductors; consider thermal limits, memory errors, latency under load, power supply.
requirements.author: Catalogue author
requirements.notes: Derived requirement (rule A8), stand-alone (D0026).

requirements.title: Vulnerability of the model to hardware faults evaluated by fault injection
requirements.statement: Where relevant for the network type and integrity level, the vulnerability of the AI model to random hardware faults (e.g. soft errors) is evaluated by fault injection, the share of faults leading to unsafe behaviour is determined with statistical confidence, vulnerable parts are protected and the results feed the hardware safety analysis.
requirements.acceptance_criterion: Justification of applicability; fault model (locations, bit positions, data types, transient/permanent); injection campaign size and confidence; outcomes classified (masked, safe, detected, unsafe) against the safety requirement; protection of vulnerable parts (ECC, range checks, selective redundancy); results used in hardware metrics.
requirements.assessor_guidance: Outcomes are judged by the safety requirement (e.g. person missed in protective zone), not by average accuracy.
requirements.author: Catalogue author
requirements.notes: Derived requirement (rule A8), stand-alone (D0026).

requirements.title: Safety-relevant decision logic kept outside the ML model
requirements.statement: The architecture tolerates failures of the AI component without loss of safety; safety-relevant decision logic is implemented outside the ML model as conventional, traceable software where practicable.
requirements.acceptance_criterion: Architecture rationale showing the partitioning between ML model and conventional safety logic; residual decisions inside the model justified.
requirements.assessor_guidance: Example: the model only delivers detections; zone assignment, distance evaluation and the stop decision are conventional software.
requirements.author: Catalogue author
requirements.notes: Derived requirement (rule A8), stand-alone (D0026).

requirements.title: Safety functions specified
requirements.statement: Each safety function is specified (function, response, safe state, timing) with the integrity level required by the risk assessment, so that the control system prevents hazardous situations.
requirements.acceptance_criterion: Safety requirements specification per safety function.
requirements.author: Catalogue author

requirements.title: No unexpected start
requirements.statement: No unexpected start occurs, including on control faults and on interruption or restoration of power or network connection.
requirements.acceptance_criterion: Fault-injection and power-cycle tests without unexpected start.
requirements.author: Catalogue author

requirements.title: No uncontrolled parameter change
requirements.statement: Parameters do not change in an uncontrolled way where this could lead to hazardous situations, incl. after power/network disturbances.
requirements.acceptance_criterion: Parameter integrity checks and tests.
requirements.author: Catalogue author

requirements.title: Stopping not impeded
requirements.statement: Stopping is not prevented once a stop command has been given, and automatic or manual stopping is unimpeded.
requirements.acceptance_criterion: Stop-path tests incl. AI component failure states.
requirements.author: Catalogue author

requirements.title: Protective devices remain effective or stop
requirements.statement: Protective devices remain fully effective or give a stop command, incl. after faults and power/network disturbances.
requirements.acceptance_criterion: Tests show detection remains effective or a stop is issued.
requirements.author: Catalogue author

requirements.title: Coherent safety functions in assemblies
requirements.statement: Safety-related parts of the control system apply coherently to the whole assembly of machinery.
requirements.acceptance_criterion: Integration description shows coverage of all hazardous zones/movements by the safety function.
requirements.author: Catalogue author

requirements.title: Foreseeable human errors tolerated
requirements.statement: Reasonably foreseeable human errors during operation do not lead to hazardous situations.
